title: Domains and common fraction field for monoid algebras
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $G$ be a torsion-free abelian group, and let $Q\subseteq G$ be a finitely generated submonoid that generates $G$ as a group. The monomial map embeds $k[Q]$ into the group algebra $k[G]$; both are integral domains, and the fraction field of $k[Q]$ identifies with the fraction field of $k[G]$ (equivalently, every monomial of $k[G]$ is a quotient of two monomials from $k[Q]$). We use the monoid and group-completion conventions of [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup].

source.place: Expose VIII, Lemma 3.2.9 and the monomial-basis normalization argument, printed p.104

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-monoid-algebra-injective-map] to $R=k$ and the injective additive homomorphism $Q\hookrightarrow G$. This gives the unital monomial embedding $\iota:k[Q]\to k[G]$. We retain $\iota$ explicitly in the denominator identities, distinguishing source monomials from their images.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.2.4, Lemma 3.2.9 proof and Lemma 3.2.12 first proof paragraph, printed pp.103–104; explicit supporting algebra supplied by Q73.

proof.text: The monoid $Q$ is cancellative since it lies in $G$; if $nx=ny$ with $n>0$, then $n(x-y)=0$ in $G$, so $x=y$. With finite generation these verify the hypotheses of [lem-trf-affine-monoid-unique-sums]. Apply it to $Q$, then [lem-trf-unique-sums-algebra-domain] with $R=k,M=Q$, obtaining that $k[Q]$ is an integral domain. The unique-support coefficient is exactly the product of its two nonzero coefficients.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.2.4, Lemma 3.2.9 proof and Lemma 3.2.12 first proof paragraph, printed pp.103–104; explicit supporting algebra supplied by Q73.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-support-monoid-denominator] with $R=k$: the group-generation hypothesis is precisely its hypothesis on $Q$. For every $F\in k[G]$ it gives $b\in Q,f\in k[Q]$ with $\iota(e^b)F=\iota(f)$, and $\iota(e^b)$ is a unit with inverse $e^{-b}$. It also gives $g=a-b$ and $e^g\iota(e^b)=\iota(e^a)$ for every $g\in G$. The source monomials $e^a,e^b$ are nonzero since their indicated coefficients are $1\ne0$.

source.place: Expose VIII 3.2.4, Lemma 3.2.9 proof and Lemma 3.2.12 first proof paragraph, printed pp.103–104; explicit supporting algebra supplied by Q73.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-unit-denominator-fraction-equivalence] to $A=k[Q]$, $B=k[G]$ and $i=\iota$: step 1 gives injectivity, step 2 gives the domain $A$, and step 3 verifies the unit-denominator hypothesis with $s=e^b\in A$. Thus $B$ is a domain and $J:\operatorname{Frac}(A)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Frac}(B)$ extends $\iota$. For $F/H$ with $H
e0$, choose $\iota(e^b)F=\iota(f)$ and $\iota(e^d)H=\iota(h)$ by step 3. Substitute $(x,y,a,s,b,t)=(F,H,f,e^b,h,e^d)$ in the cited formula: $e^bh
e0$ in $A$ and $J((e^df)/(e^bh))=F/H$. For $g=a-b$ as in step 3, the same extension formula gives $J(e^a/e^b)=e^g$ in $\operatorname{Frac}(B)$, using $e^b
e0$. This explicitly realizes the monomial quotient clause in the common fraction field.
